clue.text: Fought with groom, a tough lad

parts.note: to groom hair is to comb it
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth with a tough image

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out with a stable groom and a hard young man.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy (TED) was a 1950s British youth known for drapes and brawling.
explanation.definitionFit: To have combated something is to have fought against it; the two verbs are synonyms in the past tense.

clue.text: Reconnoitre, for instance

explanation.surface: Scouting out a place, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: To case a joint is to reconnoitre it before a crime, and a case is an instance or example.

clue.text: Drink stuff up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: Gulp down a drink and fill up.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a brandy distilled from the pressed grape skins left after winemaking.

clue.text: Breaking down, used AA man to an excessive extent

indicators.note: the letters break down and are put back in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: After a car breakdown, the motoring rescue patrolman was used far too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, whose patrolmen rescue broken-down cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad nauseam is Latin for to the point of sickness, meaning done to an excessive extent.

clue.text: DJ still departs through the entrance

parts.note: even means still, as in even better

indicators.note: the letter for departs passes through the word for entrance

parts.note: ingress is an entrance or way in
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A disc jockey is still leaving by the front door.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ looks like a disc jockey; in Britain it is short for dinner jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A DJ, a dinner jacket, is formal wear for men, a kind of evening dress.

clue.text: Jack and Bill acquire American calculator

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)
a bill is an account, abbreviated AC

explanation.surface: Two men named Jack and Bill pick up an American adding machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and Bill look like two men's names; they are a sailor and an account.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads on wires used for counting, the oldest kind of calculator.

clue.text: Highest happiness for composer

explanation.surface: Supreme joy for a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Bliss is perfect joy, and Sir Arthur Bliss was an English composer, Master of the Queen's Music.

clue.text: Found fault with headings in company report it cut name out

indicators.note: headings are the first letters of the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter for name is left out of the word for cut

parts.note: incised means cut into

explanation.surface: A firm's report was criticised for removing a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes N from INCISED, leaving ICISED.
explanation.definitionFit: To criticise is to find fault with someone or something; the past tenses match.

clue.text: Sound produced by bird, musical sound — it makes an impression

indicators.note: the word for bird is said aloud and written as another word

parts.note: a cygnet is a young swan
a ring is the sound of a bell

explanation.surface: A birdsong and a musical tone leave their mark.
explanation.walkthrough: CYGNET, a young swan, sounds like SIGNET.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet ring bears a seal pressed into wax to leave an impression.

clue.text: A bounder and a hound

explanation.surface: A cad and a dog are lumped together.
explanation.definitionFit: One who springs or leaps is literally a bounder, and the springer spaniel is a breed of hunting dog.

clue.text: Pirate opposed to one leader

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against or opposed to
I is the Roman numeral for one
a king is a leader of his people

explanation.surface: A buccaneer sets himself against the sole commander.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vikings were Norse seafarers who raided coasts, sea robbers in the manner of pirates.

clue.text: Atrophy — it angered one dreadfully

indicators.note: dreadfully says the letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Wasting away made someone terribly cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophy is the wasting away of a body part, a form of decline or deterioration.

clue.text: Co-equal professional …

parts.note: Co, short for company, is a business
like means equal, as in like amounts

explanation.surface: Someone working on equal terms with others in a profession.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 15 across as one surface sentence; each clue is solved alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A businesslike manner is efficient and practical, the way a professional conducts work.

clue.text: Fickle, bold, nubile — I am sure that's true

indicators.note: fickle means changeable, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: A capricious, brazen young woman insists she is certain.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying I'll be bound is an old idiom of certainty, a confident assertion that something is so.

clue.text: Dull state one gets into, being manipulated by others

indicators.note: the state and one go inside the word for dull

parts.note: matte means dull, not glossy
RI is Rhode Island, a US state
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gloomy mood someone falls into while being pushed around by others.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is a puppet worked by strings, a being moved by others' hands.

clue.text: …will retire

explanation.surface: Continuing 12 across: a professional colleague who means to stop working.
explanation.definitionFit: To bequeath something in a will is to pass it on at death, and to retire from a room is to go away from it.

clue.text: Soldier re-reading new order :

indicators.note: putting the letters into a new order rearranges them

explanation.surface: A soldier going back over his fresh instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new order' looks like an army command; it rearranges REREADING.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is a soldier, originally one who threw grenades, now a member of a guards regiment.

clue.text: Vegetable that's grown with skill on one block

parts.note: art means skill
I is the Roman numeral for one
to choke is to block, as a pipe

explanation.surface: A vegetable raised with expertise on a single plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a vegetable whose flower head is eaten.

clue.text: Scholar, popular girl, encountered in kitchen

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar
in means fashionable or popular
Marie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An academic and a well-liked young woman bump into each other in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bain-marie is a pan of hot water for cooking gently, a utensil found in a kitchen.

clue.text: Joint promotion that's in, the can

indicators.note: the letters for that's are placed inside the word for can

parts.note: a can is a tin
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A shared publicity deal that has been finished and stored away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the can' reads as a phrase for a finished film; 'that's' is the abbreviation for that is, and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a promotion linked jointly to another product, such as a film's merchandise.

clue.text: Frumious monster set about writer short of energy

indicators.note: the word for set goes around the shortened writer

parts.note: a set of things made together is a batch

indicators.note: the writer is missing a letter, so it is taken away

parts.note: Hans Christian Andersen was a writer of fairy tales
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A ferocious beast sets upon an author who is running out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of energy' drops one letter from the Danish fairy-tale writer's surname, and 'about' wraps the word for set around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's Jabberwocky the frumious Bandersnatch is a fearsome imaginary creature to be shunned.

clue.text: Bring into service some garden rollers

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Putting garden rollers to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol someone is to sign them up, bringing them into service or membership.

clue.text: Use hand to conceal prize

explanation.surface: A conjuror's trick of hiding a prize in the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To palm a card is to hide it in the hand, and the palm is a victor's prize, as in bearing the palm.

clue.text: Employ sound timbers, that's the vital point

indicators.note: sound says a word is spoken and written as another

parts.note: crucks are the pairs of curved timbers framing a building

explanation.surface: Using solid wood is what matters most.
explanation.walkthrough: CRUCKS, curved roof timbers, sounds like CRUX; 'Employ' is the link telling us to use them.
explanation.definitionFit: The crux of a matter is its decisive or most important point.

clue.text: Leaders of union prepare to unveil radical new improvement

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Trade union chiefs get ready to reveal a sweeping new reform.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is a rise or upward change in fortunes, an improvement in a situation.

clue.text: Extinct creature is around in some form

indicators.note: the letters are put into some other form, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A creature died out, yet it survives in some shape or other.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinosaurs are reptiles that died out millions of years ago, the best-known extinct animals.

clue.text: You may see a river run thus

definitions.text: You may see a river run thus

parts.words: You may see a river run thus
parts.note: still waters run in a profound way, and the river Dee followed by ply (run, as a ferry plies) builds the word

explanation.surface: Watching how a river flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep river flows profoundly, and the river Dee plus ply, to run back and forth, spells the adverb.

clue.text: Stir during period of imprisonment I'll get cross

parts.note: in means during, as in in the night
a term is a prison sentence
the I of I'll
X is a cross

explanation.surface: A prisoner, during a spell inside, will become angry.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir is slang for prison, but here it is the verb to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermix things is to mix them together, which is what stirring does.
